Despite having no realistic path to winning, Binface put in a respectable showing, finishing second with roughly 9,455 votes to Farage's 22,239.
A Bigger Win Than His Original Election

Farage's vote count actually came in about 1,000 higher than what he received when he first won the seat in the 2024 general election, giving him grounds to frame the result as a personal endorsement rather than a mere formality. Turnout was higher than many expected too, with roughly 44 percent of eligible voters in the constituency casting a ballot despite the contest falling in the middle of the summer holiday season and on one of the hottest days of the year.

Speaking to supporters after the result was announced, Farage described the win as proof that voters in Clacton had rejected what he called the political establishment's attempt to sideline him. He did not attend the official overnight vote count in person, citing security advice from local police, choosing instead to celebrate with supporters at a separate event.
The Investigation Isn't Over

While the election victory secures Farage's return to the House of Commons, it doesn't make his legal troubles disappear. The parliamentary standards investigation into the undisclosed donation, which had been paused when he stepped down, resumed within hours of the result being confirmed. That means Farage returns to Parliament with the same cloud hanging over him that prompted his resignation in the first place, only now with a fresh electoral mandate to point to if the pressure builds further.
Why It Matters Beyond Clacton

Farage has long been one of the most consequential figures in modern British politics, having played a central role in the campaign for Britain to leave the European Union and, more recently, in building Reform UK into a party some pollsters now see as a genuine contender for power. His byelection strategy, essentially daring his opponents not to show up and then claiming vindication when they don't, is a tactic that could resurface again if his finances continue to draw scrutiny.

For now, though, Farage returns to Westminster with a larger vote share, a fresh talking point about establishment parties refusing to face him at the ballot box, and an unresolved investigation still working its way through Parliament's standards process. Whether the episode ends up strengthening his political standing or simply delaying a harder reckoning with the allegations against him is likely to become clearer in the months ahead.

title: San Francisco Rents Have Overtaken New York, And The AI Boom Is Why
excerpt: San Francisco has quietly become the most expensive rental market in America, with average rents climbing 18 percent in under two years as AI companies flood the city with high-paying jobs and squeeze an already tight housing supply.
body: For years, San Francisco lived in New York City's shadow when it came to bragging rights for the most punishing rental market in the country. That has now changed. According to data from real estate firm CoStar, the average asking rent in San Francisco has climbed roughly 18 percent in under two years, pushing the city past New York to claim the title of most expensive major rental market in the United States.

The driver behind the surge isn't a mystery. It's the same force reshaping large parts of the American economy right now: artificial intelligence. Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have been expanding rapidly in the Bay Area, hiring aggressively and paying salaries that increasingly resemble Wall Street compensation packages rather than typical tech-industry pay.
Where The Money Is Landing

The rent increases haven't been spread evenly across the city. Neighborhoods closest to major AI offices, particularly SoMa and Mission Bay near OpenAI's headquarters, have seen rents climb well above 10 percent year over year, while more residential parts of the city have moved far less. Nearby Silicon Valley cities with heavy concentrations of tech offices, including Mountain View, Palo Alto and Sunnyvale, are experiencing similarly steep increases.

Analysts have compared the pattern to what New York went through in the 2000s as Wall Street rebuilt itself around hedge funds, where new wealth concentrated tightly around specific zip codes before pulling up prices in the surrounding area. Unlike the last major tech boom, though, this new wave of money isn't spreading out into the suburbs. It's staying put in the city itself, in part because AI companies have been pushing for more in-office and hybrid work rather than fully remote arrangements.
Supply Hasn't Kept Up

On the other side of the equation is a supply problem that has been building for years. San Francisco's apartment vacancy rate has fallen to roughly 3 percent in the most sought-after neighborhoods, down from around 13 percent in 2020, according to real estate tracking firms. New housing construction has slowed to a crawl in the city, meaning even a modest increase in demand from well-paid new residents translates quickly into sharply higher prices.

One senior researcher at CoStar likened the current rental market to a pressure cooker heating up fast, a description that tracks with reports of prospective tenants offering above asking rent, paying several months in advance, and in some cases submitting personal biographies to landlords in an effort to stand out in a crowded field of applicants.
Even Six-Figure Salaries Aren't Enough

Perhaps the most striking part of the story is who's being squeezed. It isn't just entry-level workers or people outside the tech industry struggling to keep up. Reports have highlighted tech employees earning around $200,000 a year who say they are still being priced out of desirable neighborhoods, with some choosing to relocate to outlying areas like Lake Tahoe rather than continue competing for housing in the city.

Some AI startups have responded by offering their own workarounds. A handful of companies now provide monthly rent stipends to employees who choose to live within walking distance of the office, arguing that shorter commutes translate into happier, more productive teams. It's a small-scale fix for a much larger structural problem, but it illustrates just how central housing costs have become to hiring conversations in the AI industry.
A Familiar Story With A New Name

San Francisco has been one of the most expensive cities in America for well over a decade, so the underlying dynamics here aren't entirely new. What's changed is the scale and speed of the latest wave, driven almost entirely by a single industry pouring enormous amounts of capital and talent into a relatively small geographic footprint. With several AI companies still expanding and additional public offerings expected in the sector, there's little indication the pressure on San Francisco's housing market is going to ease anytime soon.

title: Belgium Is Fighting Its Largest Wildfire On Record, And It's Still Not Under Control
excerpt: A wildfire tearing through Belgium's High Fens nature reserve has scorched more than 27 square kilometers, forced hundreds to evacuate, and pulled in emergency crews and aircraft from across the European Union.
body: Firefighters in eastern Belgium are battling the largest wildfire the country has recorded in its modern history, with the blaze having burned through more than 27 square kilometers of protected nature reserve as of Sunday and showing no signs of being fully contained.

The fire broke out on Friday in the High Fens, a vast nature reserve of peatlands and pine forest near the German border, and spread rapidly through the following days as hot, dry conditions fed the flames. By Saturday evening, officials in the Liège province said the fire had already scorched around 2,700 hectares, up sharply from roughly 1,600 hectares earlier the same day.
Hundreds Told To Leave Their Homes

As shifting winds pushed smoke into nearby communities, authorities ordered around 600 residents in the municipalities of Waimes and Bütgenbach to evacuate. Tourists in the area were also advised to leave, and a nearby gymnasium was opened to house people displaced by the fire. Local officials warned that unnecessary traffic in the area could hamper the movement of emergency vehicles and complicate an already difficult firefighting effort.

Liège's provincial governor said more than 250 emergency personnel had been deployed to fight the blaze, including over 100 firefighters from both Belgium and neighboring Germany, alongside police, military units and civil protection staff.
Europe Steps In

Given the scale of the fire, Belgium activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism to bring in outside help. Helicopters and water-bomber aircraft were deployed from Czechia, Sweden and the Netherlands to assist Belgian crews already on the ground, underscoring just how significant the blaze has become relative to the country's usual firefighting capacity.

A spokesperson for the regional authorities in Wallonia said the fire had not yet been brought under control as of the weekend, and cautioned that the terrain itself was making the job harder. Much of the affected area consists of difficult-to-access peatland and dense forest, conditions that limit how directly emergency crews can approach the flames.
The Worst Since 1911

Officials have described the current blaze as Belgium's largest wildfire in modern memory, far surpassing a 2011 fire in the same region that had previously held the record after burning close to 14 square kilometers. Historical accounts point to a comparable fire in 1911, during a similarly extreme period of heat and drought, as the last time this particular landscape saw destruction on this scale.

Officials cited unusually dry soil conditions this year as a key factor in why the fire has spread faster and burned deeper than the historical comparison from 2011, even though both blazes struck the same general area.
Part Of A Wider Pattern

The Belgian fire comes amid a broader run of extreme heat and wildfire activity across Western Europe this summer, with France, England and other parts of the continent also dealing with record temperatures and elevated fire risk in recent weeks. For a country not typically associated with large-scale wildfires, the scale of the High Fens blaze has become a stark example of how climate-driven extremes are increasingly showing up in places that historically haven't had to plan for them.

As of Sunday, firefighters remained focused on containment rather than declaring the fire under control, with authorities continuing to monitor wind patterns that could either help crews gain ground or push the blaze toward populated areas nearby.

title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Is Rewriting The Box Office Record Books
excerpt: Tom Holland's fourth solo outing as Spider-Man has smashed opening-weekend records, crossed a billion dollars faster than almost any film in history, and is now on pace to challenge the highest-grossing movies ever made.
body: It's been a big month for Spider-Man, and an even bigger one for Sony and Marvel Studios. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," the fourth solo film starring Tom Holland as Peter Parker, has spent the past several weeks demolishing box office records at a pace that has genuinely surprised industry watchers, even ones who expected the film to perform well.

The film opened to a record-breaking $360 million domestically, edging out "Avengers: Endgame" for the biggest opening weekend in North American box office history. It also set the all-time record for domestic preview screenings at $74.5 million, topping Endgame's previous mark, and delivered the highest-grossing Monday ever recorded, beating a longstanding "Black Panther" benchmark.
The Fastest Billion In Years

Global audiences responded just as enthusiastically. "Brand New Day" crossed $1 billion worldwide in only six days, making it the second-fastest film in history to hit that milestone, trailing only "Avengers: Endgame," which reached the same number in five days back in 2019. From there, the film kept climbing, passing $700 million domestically and $1 billion internationally within a matter of weeks, a combination that pushed its worldwide total past $1.6 billion.

That international haul alone was enough to make "Brand New Day" Sony's biggest release ever overseas, surpassing even "Spider-Man: No Way Home," which had held that title since its 2021 release. With its current trajectory, "Brand New Day" is now the 12th highest-grossing film of all time worldwide, and industry analysts believe it has a real shot at joining the small group of films that have crossed $2 billion globally, a club that currently includes just seven movies, among them "Avatar," "Titanic" and "Avengers: Endgame."
Why It's Connecting

Marvel had been coming off a stretch of comparatively underwhelming releases before "Brand New Day" arrived, which made the scale of its success even more notable within the industry. Sony's motion pictures chairman pointed to something simpler than superhero spectacle to explain the film's global appeal, framing it as a story fundamentally about friendship and connection that resonates regardless of where audiences are watching it.

Much of the pre-release buzz also centered on the real-life star power of its two leads. Tom Holland and Zendaya, who are married, generated what analytics firm RelishMix described as a record combined social media following heading into the film's release, spanning platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. Industry marketers have credited that off-screen chemistry, paired with the pair's relatively private personal lives, with fueling intense fan curiosity that translated directly into ticket sales.
Part Of A Historic Summer

"Brand New Day" isn't carrying the summer alone. It arrived alongside Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey," which has also performed strongly and became the highest-grossing film of Nolan's career after crossing $1.1 billion globally. Together, the two films have helped push the 2026 summer box office toward $4 billion domestically, a benchmark Hollywood hasn't consistently hit since before the pandemic reshaped moviegoing habits.

Including other 2026 hits like "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie," "Michael," and "Toy Story 5," this year has already produced more billion-dollar films than any year since 2019, when nine movies crossed that threshold. Industry estimates now suggest total domestic box office revenue for 2026 could top $10 billion for the first time since then, buoyed further by upcoming late-year releases like "Dune: Part Three" and "Avengers: Doomsday."
What Comes Next

With minimal major competition left on the summer release calendar, "Brand New Day" is expected to keep adding to its totals well into the fall, driven by repeat viewings from longtime fans and steady word-of-mouth. Whether it ultimately catches "No Way Home's" full run of $1.9 billion or pushes into the $2 billion range remains to be seen, but its opening weeks alone have already secured its place among the biggest theatrical releases in recent memory.

title: Spotify Will Start Labeling AI-Generated Artists With a New 'AI Persona' Badge
excerpt: Starting in mid-September, Spotify will flag artist profiles that represent AI-generated identities and exclude them from algorithmic recommendations by default, in one of the music industry's most direct moves yet against synthetic artists.
body: Spotify announced this week that it will begin labeling artist profiles with a new "AI Persona" badge starting in mid-September, targeting cases where an artist's public identity — rather than necessarily the music itself — appears to be entirely AI-generated. The badge will show up on the artist's profile page, in relevant search results, and within playlist track listings, giving listeners a clear signal when they're following an act that isn't actually a real person.

Crucially, Spotify says the distinction is about identity, not production process. An artist who uses AI tools somewhere in their songwriting or production workflow won't automatically be flagged; the badge is reserved specifically for profiles where the artist's name and imagery represent a photorealistic AI-generated persona rather than a real human being building a career in music.
How It Will Work

Spotify says it won't rely solely on artists disclosing their own AI status, though the platform will let artists voluntarily identify as AI Personas through Spotify for Artists. The company will also actively review profiles itself, using detection methods to flag cases it believes represent synthetic identities. Artists who are flagged will be notified and given a chance to appeal if they believe the label was applied incorrectly.

Perhaps the most consequential part of the announcement is that AI Persona profiles will be excluded from Spotify's editorial and algorithmic recommendations by default, meaning they won't appear in playlists like Discover Weekly or Release Radar unless a listener has specifically chosen to follow them. Since those recommendation systems are often the primary way independent artists without major label backing reach new listeners, the change effectively narrows AI Personas' path to organic growth while leaving their music fully accessible to anyone who seeks it out directly.
Part of a Bigger Industry Push

The move builds on a broader Artist Identity & Trust initiative Spotify has been rolling out over the past year, including verification badges, AI-generated music detection tools, and protections against unauthorized AI voice clones and deepfakes. It also arrives shortly after the EU AI Act's transparency requirements for AI-generated audio became enforceable across all 27 member states on August 2, and about a month after a coalition including the RIAA and IFPI proposed voluntary AI labeling standards for streaming platforms industry-wide.

The policy follows growing listener discomfort with synthetic acts, most notably the controversy around The Velvet Sundown, an AI-generated band that racked up millions of streams last year while posing as a real group, even landing on algorithmic playlists with hundreds of thousands of followers. In its announcement, Spotify said its programming is focused on elevating music from authentic artists building real careers, framing the new badge as a matter of basic transparency rather than a judgment on AI as a creative tool.

title: Europe's First Total Solar Eclipse in Nearly Three Decades Draws Massive Crowds
excerpt: The August 12 total solar eclipse plunged parts of Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain into daytime darkness, marking the first total eclipse over mainland Europe since 1999.
body: Crowds gathered across northern Spain, Iceland and Greenland on August 12 to witness the year's only total solar eclipse, an event that marked the first total eclipse visible from mainland Europe since 1999 and the first seen from continental European Union territory since 1999. The path of totality traced a dramatic route starting over Siberia, arcing across the North Pole, down the eastern coast of Greenland, past western Iceland, and finally across the Atlantic to fade out over northern Spain just before sunset.

Totality lasted less than two minutes for most viewers positioned directly in the Moon's shadow, but the effect was striking wherever it occurred: skies went fully dark in the middle of the day, temperatures noticeably dropped, and in several locations observers reported animals reacting as though night had suddenly fallen. Cities including A Coruña, Valencia, Zaragoza, Palma and Bilbao fell within the path of totality, while both Madrid and Barcelona sat just outside it, leaving those cities with only a deep partial eclipse.
Watched Across Two Continents

While the total eclipse itself was confined to a narrow band, a much wider partial eclipse was visible across a huge swath of the Northern Hemisphere, including all of Europe, North Africa, parts of Asia, and much of North America. In the United States, the partial eclipse was visible primarily in northern and northeastern states, with cities like Boston, Philadelphia, Washington D.C. and Portland catching a modest bite taken out of the Sun in the early afternoon hours.

Because the eclipse occurred just over two days after the Moon reached its closest point to Earth this month, its apparent size was slightly larger than average, intensifying the darkness experienced during totality. NASA and the European Space Agency both released detailed path maps ahead of the event, and safety officials repeatedly urged the public to use certified eclipse glasses meeting the ISO 12312-2 standard for any direct viewing outside the brief window of full totality.
Looking Ahead to the Next One

Total solar eclipses occur roughly every 18 months somewhere on Earth, but any single location typically waits centuries between events. Europe won't have to wait nearly that long for its next one: a total solar eclipse is set to cross Spain, North Africa and the Middle East on August 2, 2027, followed by an annular eclipse visible from South America, Portugal and Spain in January 2028.

For American eclipse chasers, the wait is considerably longer. The next total solar eclipse to touch US soil won't arrive until 2044, and even then it will only be visible from Montana, North Dakota and South Dakota, with a more widely accessible coast-to-coast eclipse not expected again until 2045.

title: Pakistan End Three-Year Overseas Test Drought With Series-Levelling Win Over West Indies
excerpt: Babar Azam's return as Test captain got off to a winning start as Pakistan bounced back from a first-Test defeat to level the series 1-1, powered by centuries from Abdullah Shafique and Babar himself.
body: Pakistan salvaged a share of their two-match Test series against the West Indies, bouncing back from a 90-run defeat in the opening Test in Tarouba to win the second Test in Port of Spain by eight wickets, sealing the series 1-1. The result marked Pakistan's first away Test win in three years, snapping an eight-match losing streak on foreign soil.

Chasing a modest target of 75 in the second innings, Pakistan made light work of the run chase despite losing early wickets to Jayden Seales and a mix-up that saw Azan Awais edge onto his stumps. Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique, the two batting heroes of Pakistan's first innings, steadied the chase before Babar danced down the wicket to smash Jomel Warrican for successive sixes and seal the win shortly after lunch on the fourth day.
Shafique and Babar Lead the Way

Abdullah Shafique was named Player of the Match after a match haul of 160 not out and 24 not out, anchoring Pakistan's total in the first innings and guiding them home unbeaten in the chase. Babar Azam, playing his second stint as Pakistan's Test captain, finished the series with 193 runs and was named Player of the Series, capping a strong personal comeback with both bat and leadership.

West Indies all-rounder Justin Greaves had an outstanding series of his own, finishing with 111 runs and seven wickets and earning Player of the Series honors for the home side, a reflection of how competitive the two-match series proved despite the lopsided nature of the second Test's finish.
A Familiar Scoreline

The 1-1 result extends a curious pattern between the two sides, marking the third consecutive Test series between Pakistan and West Indies to end in a drawn scoreline. Pakistan's spin attack, led by Sajid Khan and supported by pace bowlers Mohammad Ali and Mohammad Abbas, did much of the heavy lifting across the series, while the tourists made several changes to their bowling combinations as they searched for the right balance overseas.

With the series now behind them, Pakistan will look to carry the momentum into their upcoming tour of England, where they are set to play three Tests between August 19 and September 13 as part of the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. The overseas win in Port of Spain offers a timely confidence boost ahead of what promises to be a much sterner test in English conditions.

title: Oil Prices Stay Volatile as Strait of Hormuz Talks Between the US and Iran Drag On
excerpt: Crude prices have swung wildly for weeks as negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz repeatedly stall, with roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply still bottlenecked by the ongoing standoff.
body: Oil markets remain on edge as negotiations between the United States and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz continue to stall, with Brent crude swinging between roughly $78 and $90 a barrel over the past two weeks alone. The strait, a chokepoint that normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil supply, has seen traffic collapse to a fraction of pre-conflict levels since fighting broke out between the US, Israel and Iran earlier this year.

Ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic showed only eight to fifteen vessels crossing the strait on some recent days, compared with roughly 130 transits before the conflict began. The disruption has been described by analysts as the largest energy supply shock in recorded history, forcing tankers to either wait indefinitely or turn back entirely rather than risk passage through contested waters.
A Deal That Keeps Slipping Away

The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding back on June 17 aimed at reopening Hormuz to commercial shipping, but the agreement collapsed almost immediately as fighting resumed over which specific routes vessels would be allowed to use. Iran has continued to demand that ships sail through its territorial waters when transiting the strait, while the US has maintained a naval blockade in response to renewed attacks on tankers.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested in early August that a breakthrough deal could arrive within days, and President Trump has repeatedly signaled that talks were close to a resolution. But each round of optimism has been followed by setbacks: Iranian state media published a restrictive draft proposal that would ban US and Israeli vessels outright and impose steep penalties on other nations it accuses of wrongdoing, while Iran's foreign ministry has separately demanded that Washington lift its naval blockade and pay war reparations before any deal can proceed.
What It Means for Prices

The back-and-forth has kept traders on edge, with Brent crude still up roughly 16% to 24% compared with levels before the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February. The US Energy Information Administration does not expect Middle East oil production to return to anywhere near pre-conflict levels until early 2027, and projects Brent will average around $87 a barrel for the year.

Analysts warn that further escalation, including any new Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure or a sustained deadlock in talks, could send prices sharply higher again. For now, markets are stuck in a holding pattern, reacting to every fresh headline out of Washington, Tehran and Muscat, where Iran and Oman continue separate negotiations over how shipping through the strait might eventually resume.

title: Record-Breaking Climber Nirmal Purja Killed in Avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak
excerpt: The Nepali mountaineer who once scaled all 14 of the world's highest peaks in record time died alongside nine others when an avalanche swept their expedition off Broad Peak in Pakistan's Karakoram range.
body: World-renowned mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja has died in an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak, the world's 12th-highest mountain, along with nine other members of his expedition. Purja, 43, and his team were struck while attempting the technically demanding 26,414-foot peak in the Karakoram mountain range in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region on July 30.

The avalanche swept the ten climbers down the mountain's main west-facing gulley, in some cases carrying them nearly a vertical mile. A rescue and recovery mission launched immediately, with military helicopters and ground teams from the Alpine Club of Pakistan searching the difficult terrain, but officials confirmed by August 1 that Purja and the rest of the group had not survived.
A Legendary Climbing Career

Purja rose to global fame in 2019 when he became the first person to summit all 14 of the world's mountains above 8,000 meters in just six months and six days, a feat that had previously been expected to take years. His achievement, chronicled in the Netflix documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, turned the former British special forces soldier into one of the most recognizable figures in mountaineering, known for his charisma as much as his climbing records.

Before turning to elite mountaineering, Purja served with the Nepal-born Gurkhas and later in Britain's Special Boat Service, where regulations prevented him from discussing his deployments in detail, though he said he took part in every theater of conflict Britain was involved in during his service. He founded the Nimsdai Foundation in 2022 to support Nepal's Sherpa community, a group he frequently credited for making high-altitude mountaineering possible.
A Dangerous Recovery Effort

Recovering the bodies has proven extremely difficult given ongoing avalanche risk on the mountain. Pakistani climber Sirbaz Khan, the first Pakistani to summit all 14 eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen, told reporters that rescue teams were dealing with two or three additional avalanches every day as they worked to locate and retrieve the climbers. Purja's body was eventually located, though as of early August it remained stuck in a dangerous section of the mountain that rescuers had not yet been able to safely reach.

Tributes poured in from across the climbing world and beyond, including from UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting, who said he was deeply saddened by the loss. The Nimsdai Foundation said in a statement that Purja's legacy would live on through the countless people he inspired to pursue their own version of the impossible.

title: Aubrey Plaza Welcomes Her First Baby With Christopher Abbott
excerpt: The Parks and Recreation and White Lotus star is officially a first-time mom, giving birth to a baby girl more than a year after the loss of her husband, Jeff Baena.
body: Aubrey Plaza is officially a mother. The actress welcomed her first child, a baby girl, with partner Christopher Abbott during the last week of July, according to sources close to the couple. Plaza was spotted in New York City on August 9 holding her newborn while attending Abbott's final performance in the Broadway revival of Death of a Salesman, marking the first public sighting of the baby.

The pregnancy first came to light in dramatic fashion back in April, when Plaza casually revealed the news during an appearance on the Smartless podcast, telling hosts Will Arnett, Jason Bateman and Sean Hayes, "There's a baby inside me," while recounting a doctor's visit. A representative for Plaza later confirmed the pregnancy to People, describing it as a beautiful surprise following an emotionally difficult year.
A New Chapter After Loss

The baby's arrival comes roughly 18 months after the death of Plaza's estranged husband, filmmaker Jeff Baena, who died by suicide in January 2025. Plaza and Baena had quietly separated in the months before his death, and the news drew an outpouring of support alongside some public reflection on how quickly her life had changed in the time since.

Plaza and Abbott's relationship grew out of a long professional partnership. The pair first worked together on the 2020 Sundance thriller Black Bear and later reunited for an off-Broadway revival of Danny and the Deep Blue Sea in 2023. They made their red carpet debut as a couple at the 2026 Tony Awards, where Abbott was nominated for his role in Death of a Salesman, before confirming the pregnancy publicly just weeks later.
Keeping It Private

True to form for two famously private actors, Plaza and Abbott have said little publicly about the pregnancy or birth beyond the initial confirmations, and neither has commented directly on the baby's arrival. Plaza did make a point of showing off her baby bump at Paris Fashion Week in March, sitting front row at the Loewe show in an oversized leather jacket, before mostly staying out of the spotlight as her due date approached.

For Plaza, 41, best known for her breakout role as April Ludgate on Parks and Recreation and more recent turns in The White Lotus and Ingrid Goes West, the new arrival marks a deeply personal milestone in a year that has otherwise kept her largely out of the public eye.

title: England Survive 10-Goal Thriller to Beat France 6-4 and Claim World Cup Bronze
excerpt: Bukayo Saka's hat-trick powered England to their best World Cup finish since 1966, in a wild third-place match that saw them blow a four-goal lead before holding on in Miami.
body: England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 with a stunning 6-4 win over France in the tournament's third-place playoff at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium, capping the highest-scoring men's World Cup knockout match since 1954. Bukayo Saka's hat-trick was the headline act, but the game will be remembered as much for England nearly squandering a commanding four-goal cushion as for the individual brilliance on display.

England raced into a 4-0 halftime lead that looked to have the match well in hand. Declan Rice opened the scoring in just the third minute with a curling strike from distance, one of the earliest goals in England's World Cup history, before assisting Ezri Konsa's header from a corner. Saka then struck twice before the break, first tapping in from a Marcus Rashford pass and then finishing sharply from the edge of the box.
France's Second-Half Fightback

France, who had looked disinterested for most of the first half, transformed after the restart. Kylian Mbappé pulled a goal back in the 48th minute before Bradley Barcola made it 4-2, and Mbappé struck again in the 66th to suddenly put France within one goal, sending nerves through the England camp. Saka restored some breathing room with a penalty to complete his hat-trick, but Ousmane Dembélé's late strike in stoppage time made it 5-4 and set up a tense finish.

Jude Bellingham finally settled the match in the eighth minute of stoppage time, dribbling past three French defenders inside the box before slotting home to make it 6-4 and confirm England's bronze medal. Mbappé's brace in the match also made him the World Cup's all-time leading scorer, adding another individual milestone to a night already packed with them.
A Historic Finish for England

The result gives England their best World Cup finish on foreign soil and their highest placing overall since lifting the trophy on home turf in 1966. Saka became only the second England player, after Sir Geoff Hurst, to score a hat-trick in a World Cup knockout match, and just the second player in tournament history to do so against France, joining Brazil's Pelé, who managed the feat in 1958.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel, who had heard boos from sections of England fans before kickoff following a difficult tournament, struck a measured tone in his post-match press conference, noting that the medal was England's first at a World Cup in 60 years even as he acknowledged the semifinal exit to Argentina still stung. With France's Didier Deschamps set to hand the reins to Zinedine Zidane before the 2028 Euros on home soil, both sides now turn toward rebuilding for the next major tournament cycle.

title: Andrew and Tristan Tate Arrested in Miami as UK Pursues Extradition on Dozens of New Charges
excerpt: The controversial influencer brothers were taken into custody by US Marshals after British prosecutors filed dozens of additional charges, testing the limits of their political connections in Washington.
body: Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested by US Marshals in Miami on July 18 after British prosecutors filed a fresh wave of charges against them, triggering a UK extradition request that is now working its way through US courts. The dual British-American citizens are being held in a Florida prison as they fight to avoid being sent back to the United Kingdom.

The UK's Crown Prosecution Service said the new charges bring the total number of alleged offenses against the brothers to 59, spanning seven victims and covering conduct authorities say occurred between 2010 and 2017 in the East of England region. Andrew Tate faces the larger share of the charges, including counts of rape, trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault, and offenses tied to indecent images of a child. Tristan Tate faces a smaller number of charges covering sexual assault, rape, and trafficking.
A Long-Running Legal Saga

This is far from the Tates' first brush with the law. The brothers were first detained in Romania in December 2022 over a separate human trafficking investigation, which led to a criminal indictment in 2023 accusing them of running an organized crime operation built around exploiting women. That Romanian case has dragged on for years, with Andrew Tate recently losing an appeal to relax the judicial restrictions he's been living under while the trial continues.

The brothers have denied all wrongdoing throughout, and their attorney told reporters following the Miami arrest that they intend to contest the UK's extradition request. Assistant Chief Constable Karena Thomas of Bedfordshire Police, whose major crime unit led the investigation behind the new charges, said the case reflected close cooperation between national and international law enforcement agencies.
Testing Political Ties

The arrest carries an added layer of intrigue given the Tates' visibility within pro-Trump online circles. Andrew Tate has built a following among prominent voices on the American right, and the brothers were seen attending events alongside senior US officials as recently as this spring. But when the UK's extradition request landed, the Trump administration signaled it would not intervene, with White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt issuing a brief statement in July confirming there were no plans to step in on the brothers' behalf.

That response marked a notable shift for a movement that had previously embraced the Tates as symbols of a broader cultural fight, and it left several of their past political allies conspicuously quiet. Only a small number of figures, including Rep. Abe Hamadeh of Arizona, publicly pushed back against the extradition effort.

The brothers are scheduled to continue fighting the extradition request in Florida federal court, a process that legal experts say could stretch on for months. For now, they remain in custody as both the US and UK legal systems work through one of the more closely watched extradition battles in recent memory.

title: Colombia's Earthquake Death Toll Passes 265 as Rescue Crews Race Against Time
excerpt: The strongest earthquake to hit Colombia this century has killed more than 265 people and left thousands more injured or missing, testing a brand-new government just days into office.
body: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake that tore through western Colombia on Monday has become the deadliest the country has seen this century, with the death toll climbing past 265 as rescue crews continue digging through collapsed buildings four days later. More than 3,700 people have been injured and over 4,100 remain reported missing, according to figures compiled by Colombian authorities and tracked through the week.

The quake struck near San José del Palmar in the department of Chocó, an underdeveloped stretch of western Colombia roughly 150 miles from Bogotá, at a depth of about 103 kilometers. Tremors were felt as far away as neighboring Ecuador and Panama, but the worst destruction hit Cali, Pereira, Quibdó and Manizales, where entire blocks of buildings pancaked to the ground within seconds.
A New President's Baptism by Fire

The disaster landed just days after Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, forcing him to lead national emergency response efforts before completing his first week in office. He declared a state of national disaster almost immediately, deployed soldiers to the hardest-hit areas, and has since toured cities in the country's coffee region to announce economic relief measures for affected families.

Among the most harrowing scenes was the collapse of the pediatric and neonatal wings of a hospital in Cali, one of several medical facilities damaged in the quake. A jail fire broke out in nearby Buenaventura as a direct result of the tremor, killing at least four inmates and sending two more to the hospital. Colombia's Geological Service has since recorded more than 70 aftershocks across the country, complicating an already difficult rescue effort.
Racing Against the Clock

Search-and-rescue teams, including international crews from Mexico and other regional partners, have been working around the clock in Cali and surrounding cities, at times pulling survivors from the rubble more than 30 hours after the initial quake. In Manizales, city officials say the death toll has held at five, but the volume of damage assessment requests for private homes is so high it will take at least a month to work through.

Local leaders in the hardest-hit La Italia district, near the earthquake's epicenter, describe a community still without reliable water or electricity days after the tremor, with structural damage making many buildings unsafe to re-enter. Aid convoys from regional partners began arriving in force by midweek, and international donors from the US, Europe and the Middle East have pledged support for the recovery effort.
Could It Happen Again?

Geologists say Colombia sits atop a dense network of active fault lines, and while the odds of another quake this powerful striking the same area soon are considered low, experts are not ruling out further seismic activity in the weeks ahead. The quake follows a pair of even deadlier earthquakes that struck neighboring Venezuela in June, underscoring how seismically active the region has become this year.

For now, the priority remains recovery. With thousands still unaccounted for and entire neighborhoods reduced to rubble, officials say the true scale of the disaster may not be clear for weeks, even as rescue crews hold onto hope of finding more survivors beneath the wreckage.

title: Uber and China's Pony AI Are Bringing Over 2,000 Robotaxis to Europe
excerpt: Uber is expanding its partnership with Chinese self-driving company Pony AI to deploy more than 2,000 driverless robotaxis across Europe, moving the technology from a single pilot city to full commercial scale.
body: Uber and China's Pony AI announced Friday that they are expanding their partnership to deploy more than 2,000 robotaxis across Europe, a major step up from the single commercial pilot the two companies launched in Zagreb, Croatia earlier this year. The expanded deal will bring driverless rides to four additional, still-unnamed European cities, with the companies saying rollout details will be announced in phases over the coming months.

Under the arrangement, Pony AI supplies its Level 4 autonomous driving technology along with the operational know-how it has built running robotaxi fleets across China, while Uber contributes its ride-hailing platform, handling bookings, payments and customer service. A local partner in each market will manage day-to-day fleet operations such as maintenance, cleaning and charging, meaning the robotaxi fleet itself could be owned by different companies depending on the city.
Building on a Year-Old Partnership

The collaboration between the two companies dates back to May 2025, when they first agreed to bring Pony AI's robotaxis onto the Uber app in international markets, with an initial focus on the Middle East. That partnership extended to Europe in March 2026, when Uber and Pony AI teamed up with Croatian mobility company Verne to launch what they describe as the continent's first commercial robotaxi service in Zagreb — a service that is now set to become bookable directly through the Uber app.

Pony AI CEO James Peng described the expanded deal as reflecting a shared commitment to bringing reliable robotaxi service to more European cities, while Uber's autonomous mobility leadership framed the moment as autonomous driving's shift from isolated pilot launches toward repeatable commercial scale. Pony AI already runs fully driverless, paid robotaxi services in four major Chinese cities — Beijing, Guangzhou, Shanghai and Shenzhen — where the company says it has reached breakeven economics on a city-wide basis.
Part of a Bigger Robotaxi Race

The announcement lands amid a broader scramble among ride-hailing and autonomous vehicle companies to build out fleet scale, which is increasingly seen as the key bottleneck for the robotaxi industry. More vehicles on the road mean more real-world data to prove safety to regulators, plus better utilization and lower wait times that make the service viable for everyday riders rather than a novelty.

Uber has now partnered with more than 30 autonomous vehicle companies globally as it works to embed self-driving options across its platform rather than betting on a single technology provider. The Pony AI expansion follows closely on the heels of Uber's separate tie-up with UK-based Wayve Technologies, which recently secured approval to run a supervised robotaxi service in London, adding yet another market to Uber's growing autonomous ambitions across the continent.

Both companies also confirmed plans to explore robotaxi deployment in the Middle East as part of the same expanded agreement, though specifics there remain even further out. With Europe's first named cities still to be revealed, the real test of this announcement will come once actual vehicles start appearing on the streets — something both companies say is still a matter of months, not years, away.

title: The Premier League Is Back: Community Shield Kicks Off a Blockbuster 2026-27 Season
excerpt: English football's new season opens with Arsenal defending their crown against Manchester City in the Community Shield, ahead of a record-spending summer that has reshaped nearly every top club.
body: English football's traditional curtain-raiser arrives this weekend, with reigning Premier League champions Arsenal facing FA Cup winners Manchester City in the Community Shield at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Sunday, August 16. It's the first competitive fixture of a season that kicks off a week later than usual, pushed back to accommodate player recovery time following this summer's World Cup.

The Premier League proper begins Friday, August 21, when Arsenal host newly promoted Coventry City at the Emirates in the season's headline opening fixture. The rest of the opening weekend is packed with intrigue: Manchester United travel to Hull City for a tricky opening test, two London derbies see Brentford host Tottenham and Fulham welcome Chelsea, and Newcastle close out the weekend by hosting Liverpool on Sunday night.
A Summer of Record Spending

This transfer window has been one of the most expensive in Premier League history, and few clubs have spent as aggressively as Tottenham Hotspur. Under new head coach Roberto De Zerbi, Spurs broke their transfer record twice in a matter of days, first paying West Ham £85 million for Mateus Fernandes before smashing that mark again with a £100 million deal for Newcastle midfielder Sandro Tonali. Combined, the two deals push Tottenham's summer outlay past £200 million, comfortably surpassing their previous single-window record.

Arsenal, defending their title for the first time in years, have strengthened significantly themselves, adding Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapié and Illan Meslier while narrowly missing out on Vinícius Júnior, who ultimately signed a new contract to stay at Real Madrid. Liverpool have been similarly active, bringing in Jeremy Jacquet and Víctor Muñoz on permanent deals and landing a surprise loan signing in Barcelona captain Ronald Araújo, while continuing to pursue a deal for PSG winger Bradley Barcola.
Chelsea's Big-Money Rebuild

No club has outspent Chelsea this summer, who have committed roughly €408 million combined across eleven new signings. Morgan Rogers arrived as the marquee addition at more than €135 million, while the club also added experience through the signings of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, aiming to balance a young squad with proven Premier League know-how ahead of a season where they'll be expected to challenge at the top.
What to Watch For

With the transfer window still open until August 31, more late deals are expected before the deadline, even as the season is already underway. The compressed post-World Cup calendar means squads will need depth early, with several stars, including some who featured deep into this summer's tournament in Spain and Argentina's colors, needing to manage fatigue heading into a punishing 33-weekend league schedule that runs through to May 30, 2027.

For now, all eyes turn to Cardiff on Sunday, where Arsenal and Manchester City will offer the first real glimpse of how this summer's spending spree translates onto the pitch — and set the tone for what promises to be one of the most competitive Premier League seasons in years.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo Is Married — He Secretly Wed Georgina Rodriguez in Cascais After Fans Waited Outside the Wrong Cathedral
excerpt: After days of frenzied speculation and hundreds of fans gathering at the wrong location, Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez pulled off a private wedding in Portugal that even the world's most-followed athlete managed to keep secret.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez are officially married. The couple wed in a private civil ceremony on Tuesday, August 11 in Cascais, an upscale coastal resort just west of Lisbon where the pair own a villa, according to a statement from Ronaldo's representatives at the Brunswick Group. The wedding came exactly one year after Rodríguez publicly confirmed their engagement, and it capped a relationship that began nearly a decade ago.

The confirmation followed days of frenzied public speculation across Portugal. Rumors had pointed to Funchal Cathedral in Madeira, Ronaldo's birthplace, as the wedding venue, and hundreds of fans gathered outside the cathedral on August 8 hoping to catch a glimpse of the ceremony. It turned out to belong to a completely different couple; the cathedral itself told reporters beforehand that it had no Ronaldo wedding scheduled, even as it noted hosting one would have been an honor.
How They Kept It Secret

While Portuguese media had also floated Sintra as a possible location, Ronaldo and Rodríguez ultimately chose Cascais, keeping their actual plans completely under wraps until after the ceremony had already taken place. The couple's representatives told AFP the pair specifically wanted a private event and asked that the news be shared without any additional media access. The only visual confirmation came from a single photo the couple posted to their joint social media accounts, showing their clasped hands and matching wedding bands beneath a simple caption reading "C ♡ G." The image reportedly surpassed four million likes within 40 minutes.

The ceremony was reportedly intimate and centered entirely on family, with the couple's five children in attendance: Cristiano Jr., twins Eva and Mateo, Alana Martina, and Bella Esmeralda. No other guests appear to have been invited, and there was no elaborate photo shoot or red-carpet unveiling — a notably understated approach for two of the most-followed people on the planet.
A Decade in the Making

Ronaldo and Rodríguez met in 2016 at a Gucci store in Madrid, where she was working as a sales assistant, and began dating discreetly before going public at the 2017 FIFA Awards. Their family grew quickly in the years that followed: Eva and Mateo were born via surrogacy in June 2017, and Rodríguez gave birth to Alana Martina that November. The couple also weathered profound loss together, announcing in 2022 the death of their newborn son Ángel, twin brother to daughter Bella.

Rodríguez went on to build her own public profile through the Netflix series I Am Georgina, which followed the family's life balancing football, fashion and travel, helping turn her into a media figure in her own right well beyond her relationship with Ronaldo.
What's Next for the Newlyweds

At 41, Ronaldo recently competed in a record sixth FIFA World Cup, and continues playing professionally in Saudi Arabia while building out a business empire that made him football's first billionaire, according to a Bloomberg estimate of his net worth. The wedding lands at a grounded, personal moment in a career defined by records and headlines, closing one chapter of his life just as another — a marriage nearly ten years in the making — quietly begins.

title: Kim Kardashian Shares Her Most Intimate Photos Yet With Lewis Hamilton
excerpt: During Formula 1's summer break, Kim Kardashian posted a candid new batch of photos with Lewis Hamilton — including a cozy mirror selfie — signaling the notoriously private couple is more comfortable than ever going public.
body: Kim Kardashian gave fans their clearest look yet into her relationship with Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton this week, sharing a round-up of photos from recent weeks that included several shots of the couple together during F1's mid-season summer break. The images, posted as part of a broader Instagram carousel documenting Kardashian's summer, stood out immediately to fans and entertainment outlets who have spent the better part of a year piecing together the contours of a relationship both parties have kept carefully guarded. In one frame, a mirror selfie showed the pair coordinated in relaxed brown loungewear, with Hamilton wrapping his arms around Kardashian from behind in a moment that read less like a staged red-carpet appearance and more like an ordinary Tuesday at home.

The tone of the post was notable in itself. Kardashian, who has spent close to two decades building a media empire partly on the back of documenting her personal life, has historically been far more guarded about romantic relationships once they move past the rumor stage. Her marriage to Kanye West played out almost entirely in public, but her post-divorce relationships — first with Pete Davidson, then loosely with NFL player Odell Beckham Jr. — were handled with noticeably more restraint on her own channels, even as tabloids filled in the gaps. The new photos with Hamilton represent a departure from that pattern, suggesting either a shift in how she wants to manage her public image going forward, or simply a comfort level with Hamilton that she hasn't reached with a partner in years.

Hamilton, for his part, mirrored the gesture. He posted his own carousel of images featuring Kardashian, captioning it with a simple reference to resting, restoring and recharging during the summer break — an unusually domestic sentiment from a driver whose public persona has typically centered on racing, fashion, activism and his production work rather than romance. The post followed an earlier one from Hamilton just weeks prior featuring vacation memories with Kardashian and her four children: North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7. Including her children in his own posts marked a meaningful step for a couple that had, until recently, avoided any hint of blended-family imagery.
How the Relationship Became Public

The romance first became visible to the public in February, when the two were spotted together at Estelle Manor, a luxury countryside retreat in England's Cotswolds. According to people familiar with the visit, Kardashian's arrival was deliberately low-key — she traveled with only two bodyguards and was quickly moved inside the property, away from other guests. Hamilton arrived separately by helicopter roughly an hour later. The visit reportedly included private dinners and spa treatments, the kind of low-visibility outing that suggested both parties wanted to test the relationship privately before any public confirmation.

That discretion didn't last long. Days later, the pair was spotted together in Paris, and then, most visibly, at Super Bowl LX in Santa Clara, California, where they were photographed sitting beside each other in a private suite, chatting comfortably throughout the game. The Super Bowl appearance functioned as a soft public debut: neither Kardashian nor Hamilton addressed the relationship directly, but the images circulated widely, and entertainment reporters treated the outing as effective confirmation that something serious was developing between the two.

Sources close to Kardashian described the pairing early on as unhurried. One insider told a celebrity outlet that Hamilton made her feel safe and that she was genuinely enjoying spending time with him, while another noted the comfort between them partly stemmed from the fact that the two had known each other for years within overlapping entertainment and sports circles before anything romantic developed. That kind of pre-existing familiarity is relatively unusual in Kardashian's dating history, where several of her past relationships developed quickly and publicly rather than growing out of a long-standing friendship.
A Slow Build Toward Going Public

Throughout the spring, the relationship continued to surface in smaller, quieter moments rather than grand announcements. In early March, both Kardashian and Hamilton posted strikingly similar scenic clips to their Instagram Stories from a getaway to Lake Powell in Arizona — matching water views and dusky skies, but with neither showing the other's face. It was the kind of parallel posting pattern that fans have become adept at noticing and cross-referencing, and it fueled another wave of speculation well before either party said anything definitive.

The following weeks brought further evidence. At the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscars party in March, Kardashian posted a series of photos and clips from her look for the night — a gold sequin Gucci gown paired with icy blue contact lenses. Hamilton responded in the comments with a heart-eyes emoji, a small gesture that nonetheless received thousands of likes and prompted a wave of fan reactions online, several of which treated the moment as something close to an official confirmation. It was a notably public gesture for Hamilton, who had largely avoided commenting directly on Kardashian's posts up to that point.
Two High-Profile Lives Intersecting

Both figures bring an enormous public platform to the relationship, which is part of why even small gestures — a comment, a matching photo, a joint appearance — tend to generate outsized attention. Hamilton, 41, is a seven-time Formula 1 World Champion and among the most recognizable athletes in global sports, with a career built at McLaren, Mercedes and, more recently, Ferrari. Off the track, he has become known for design collaborations, environmental and social justice advocacy, and film production work, including producing the 2025 racing film that carried his creative fingerprints across multiple award nominations.

Kardashian, 45, has built a business empire that extends well beyond her origins in reality television, anchored today by Skims, the shapewear and apparel brand she co-founded that has grown into a billion-dollar company with an increasingly broad product range spanning underwear, loungewear and swimwear. She has also continued acting work, including a recurring role in the legal drama "All's Fair," and remains one of the most consistently visible figures in celebrity culture, with a media footprint spanning television, social platforms, licensing deals and her family's long-running reality franchise.

The combination of an F1 champion and a reality-television-mogul-turned-businesswoman dating publicly places the relationship at an unusual intersection of sports and entertainment fandoms — two audiences that don't always overlap but have, in this case, been drawn into the same story. Motorsport outlets have covered the relationship largely through the lens of whether it might affect Hamilton's focus during a competitive Ferrari campaign, while entertainment press has focused more on Kardashian's dating history and what a stable relationship with a globally recognized athlete might mean for her public image going forward.
What Kardashian's Dating History Suggests About This Relationship

Kardashian's relationship history has been unusually well-documented, in part because so much of her public identity was built on sharing personal milestones. Her marriage to West produced four children and ended in a lengthy, heavily covered divorce process that concluded in 2022. She then dated "Saturday Night Live" alum Pete Davidson for roughly ten months, a relationship that played out with intense media scrutiny before ending in mid-2022. She was also loosely linked to Beckham Jr. in the period that followed, though that connection never developed into a confirmed public relationship in the way her time with Davidson did.

Compared to those previous relationships, the rollout with Hamilton has moved at a noticeably different pace. Rather than a rapid public debut, the couple spent months allowing the relationship to surface gradually through spotted outings, subtle social media parallels and a handful of high-profile appearances, only recently arriving at the kind of unguarded, affectionate photo-sharing seen this week. Entertainment commentators have read that pacing as a sign of deliberate choice on both sides — an attempt to build the relationship on more stable footing before opening it fully to public commentary.
Increasingly Comfortable in Public View

Since the Vanity Fair Oscars moment in March, the pattern has continued to build. The couple was seen together at additional high-profile events through the spring and summer, with each subsequent appearance drawing less speculation and more straightforward acknowledgment from fans and press alike that the relationship had moved past the rumor stage. The recent getaway to Lake Powell, followed by the joint vacation photos featuring Kardashian's children, and now this week's especially candid photo set, together sketch a clear trajectory: a relationship that began cautiously and has steadily become one both parties appear willing to share more openly.

Neither Kardashian nor Hamilton has issued a formal statement explicitly confirming the relationship in the traditional sense — there has been no announcement, interview or direct comment addressing its status. But the accumulation of public gestures has functioned as its own kind of confirmation, one increasingly common among high-profile couples who prefer to let their social media presence speak for them rather than sitting for interviews or issuing press statements.
What Comes Next

With Formula 1's summer break drawing to a close, attention will likely shift back toward Hamilton's on-track performance as the season resumes, particularly given the scrutiny that comes with driving for Ferrari, one of the sport's most historically demanding teams. Whether his personal life becomes a recurring storyline alongside his racing results will depend largely on how visible the relationship remains once competition resumes and both figures return to their respective full public schedules.

For Kardashian, the coming months are likely to bring continued attention to both her business ventures and her personal life in tandem, a pairing that has defined much of her career. If the current pace holds, fans should expect the relationship to continue surfacing through the same kind of organic, photo-driven glimpses that have defined it so far, rather than a single dramatic announcement — a pattern that, for a couple this well-known, may end up being the most private way of going fully public.
Hamilton's Own Relationship History

Hamilton's romantic life has, for most of his career, been considerably more private than Kardashian's, which is part of what has made this relationship feel like new territory for him as much as for her. His highest-profile past relationship was with singer Nicole Scherzinger, formerly of the Pussycat Dolls, which spanned on-and-off periods between 2007 and 2015 and was itself heavily covered by British and American tabloids given Hamilton's rising stardom in Formula 1 during that stretch. In the years since, he has been linked at various points to model Gigi Hadid, singer Rita Ora and model Barbara Palvin, though none of those connections developed into a confirmed long-term relationship in the way his time with Scherzinger did.

That relative privacy makes the current relationship with Kardashian something of a departure for Hamilton as well. Where Scherzinger-era coverage often focused on paparazzi photos and secondhand reporting, Hamilton's approach with Kardashian has involved active participation — posting his own photos, replying in comment sections, and appearing at high-visibility events without avoiding cameras. For a driver who has spent nearly two decades carefully managing how much of his personal life reaches the public, the shift suggests a level of confidence in the relationship that observers say has been evident since the Estelle Manor weekend earlier this year.
The Business Dimension

It's worth noting that both figures operate substantial commercial enterprises alongside their public personas, and a high-profile relationship inevitably intersects with those business interests, whether either party intends it to or not. Kardashian's Skims brand has increasingly leaned into celebrity collaborations and high-visibility marketing moments, and industry observers have noted that a stable, positive relationship narrative tends to complement rather than complicate that kind of brand-building. Hamilton, meanwhile, has cultivated a personal brand built around excellence, discipline and increasingly diversified business interests beyond racing, including his production company and various design and lifestyle ventures.

Neither has suggested the relationship plays any role in business decision-making, and there's no indication that any commercial collaboration between the two is planned or in progress. Still, entertainment and sports marketing analysts have pointed out that couples who occupy this much combined cultural real estate rarely keep their personal and commercial lives entirely separate for long, particularly once a relationship reaches the stage of joint family vacations and unguarded photo-sharing that this one appears to have reached.
How Fans and Media Have Responded

The reaction to this week's photos followed a familiar pattern for major celebrity relationship news: rapid spread across entertainment outlets, extensive fan commentary across social platforms, and renewed interest in every prior sighting and social media interaction between the two, reexamined now with the benefit of hindsight. Some fans expressed enthusiasm at seeing what they described as one of Kardashian's more grounded and low-drama relationships in years, particularly relative to the intense public scrutiny that characterized her marriage and subsequent high-profile dating history.

Others focused on the practical logistics of the relationship — the demands of Hamilton's F1 travel schedule, which keeps him crisscrossing the globe for roughly nine months of the year, set against Kardashian's own packed calendar of business commitments, television production and family responsibilities as a mother of four. How the couple manages that scheduling reality, largely out of public view, remains one of the more grounded questions surrounding a relationship that otherwise plays out primarily through curated social media glimpses.

As with most high-profile celebrity relationships, the full picture will likely only become clear gradually, through the accumulation of small public moments rather than any single defining statement. For now, this week's photos mark the most candid the couple has been willing to be, and offer the clearest signal yet that whatever has been building since that quiet February weekend in the Cotswolds has settled into something both Kardashian and Hamilton are comfortable letting the world see.

title: Lionel Messi's Father and Longtime Agent Jorge Messi Dies at 68
excerpt: Jorge Messi, who guided his son's career from Rosario's youth pitches to Barcelona's La Masia and eight Ballon d'Or wins, passed away Saturday after a prolonged illness he had kept private through this year's World Cup.
body: Jorge Messi, father and longtime agent of Argentine football legend Lionel Messi, died Saturday at Sanatorio Centro, a medical center in Rosario, Argentina. He was 68. The hospital's medical director confirmed his passing came in the early hours of the morning, adding that no further details about the cause of death would be shared out of respect for the family's privacy.

Newell's Old Boys, the Rosario club where a young Lionel first played before moving to Europe, announced that Jorge had been undergoing treatment for an unspecified illness in recent months. The club described him as the steady presence who, alongside his wife Celia Cuccittini, supported his son's rise with vision and care.
A Health Struggle Kept Quiet Through the World Cup

Concerns about Jorge's health first became public during this year's World Cup in North America, when Lionel grew visibly emotional after scoring in Argentina's opening match against Algeria. He later told reporters the emotion had nothing to do with football itself, describing recent weeks as difficult and complicated. The family had pushed back on premature rumors of his death at the time and asked for privacy while he received care.
The Man Behind the Career

Jorge worked as a steelworker and chemical technician before soccer took over the family's life. He'd played as a midfielder in Newell's youth ranks himself before military service cut his own playing days short. It was Jorge who traveled with a teenage Lionel to Barcelona in the early 2000s for the trial that opened the doors to La Masia, the club's famed academy, and he went on to manage his son's business affairs for two decades as Lionel won eight Ballon d'Or awards and led Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title.
Tributes Across the Football World

The Argentine Football Association ordered a minute of silence at matches nationwide, with players, coaches and referees wearing black armbands and flags lowered at AFA facilities. Barcelona thanked Jorge for entrusting the club with his son's formative years, while Real Madrid and clubs across Europe sent condolences to the family.

Jorge is survived by his wife Celia and his four children — Rodrigo, Matías, Lionel and María Sol. The loss comes just weeks after Argentina's latest World Cup campaign, and as Lionel Messi was set to return to Inter Miami's Leagues Cup fixture against Monterrey this weekend.

title: Amazon Joins the $3 Trillion Club as AWS Posts Its Fastest Growth in 18 Quarters
excerpt: A blowout earnings report sent Amazon past a $3 trillion market cap for the first time, even as founder Jeff Bezos sold roughly $4 billion of his own shares the same week.
body: Amazon became the fifth company in history to cross a $3 trillion market capitalization, joining Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Alphabet after shares jumped more than 15% in the session following its second-quarter earnings report and extended those gains the next day. The stock closed at a record $284.02, pushing the company into rarefied territory it had never reached before.

The catalyst wasn't Amazon's retail business — it was AWS. The cloud division posted $42.2 billion in quarterly revenue, growing 37% year-over-year, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, and beat Wall Street's consensus estimate by roughly $1.7 billion. Total company revenue hit $200.6 billion, up 20% from a year earlier and the first time Amazon has ever crossed $200 billion in a single quarter, while operating income jumped 43% to $27.5 billion.
A Milestone Reached Twice as Fast

Amazon needed just over two years to add its third trillion dollars in value, after taking more than six years to go from $1 trillion to $2 trillion — a gap that underscores how sharply AI-driven demand has accelerated the company's growth. AWS alone now carries a $496 billion order backlog, and CEO Andy Jassy has been vocal that AI workloads are central to the unit's momentum, even as memory costs push up spending.

The company raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to roughly $220 billion, up from an earlier forecast near $200 billion, citing continued investment in AI infrastructure and rising component costs.
Bezos Sells Into the Rally

The milestone came with an ironic twist: founder Jeff Bezos filed to sell 15 million shares worth about $4.07 billion under a pre-scheduled Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, his third such sale in just over a year following disposals in June 2025 and November 2024. CNBC's Jim Cramer summed up the mixed reaction on social media, calling the timing "a buzzkill" even while acknowledging investors couldn't fault Bezos for following a plan set months in advance.

The sale briefly rattled the stock, pulling it back about 2% from its high, though analysts widely described the move as fundamentally neutral given Bezos still holds roughly 869 million shares, or about 8.1% of the company.
What Comes Next

Wall Street remains largely bullish. JPMorgan raised its price target on Amazon to $365, and several analysts have framed the $3 trillion mark as a milestone rather than a ceiling, pointing to AWS's growing backlog and Amazon's advertising business as further catalysts. The bigger question, they note, is whether rising AI infrastructure costs can keep converting into profit at the pace investors are now pricing in.

title: Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' Crosses $1 Billion, Becomes His Highest-Grossing Film
excerpt: Matt Damon's Homeric epic has overtaken 'The Dark Knight Rises' to become Nolan's biggest box office hit ever, while fueling IMAX's best month in the company's 50-plus year history.
body: Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" has crossed the $1 billion mark at the worldwide box office, becoming the director's first film since 2012's "The Dark Knight Rises" to hit that milestone — and his highest-grossing release ever, surpassing that film's $1.08 billion total as well as 2009's "The Dark Knight" at just over $1 billion.

The nearly three-hour, R-rated adaptation of Homer's ancient poem, starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, has now taken in roughly $429.65 million domestically and $578.8 million internationally after three weeks in theaters, becoming the fifth film of 2026 to reach ten figures worldwide, following "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," "Toy Story 5," "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie" and "Michael."
A Career-Best Opening That Kept Growing

The film opened with $263.7 million worldwide, Nolan's biggest global launch of his career, and roughly half its early audience skewed between 18 and 34 years old — a notably young turnout for a nearly three-hour literary adaptation that had initially drawn skepticism given its length and rating. Made on an estimated $250 million budget, the biggest of Nolan's career, the film was shot entirely on IMAX's 70mm cameras, a first for any feature.
IMAX's Best Month Ever

That format bet has paid off handsomely for IMAX Corporation, which reported the highest-grossing month in its more than 50-year history in July, pulling in $257 million globally — 47% above its previous monthly record — largely on the back of "The Odyssey." The film has already delivered more than 24% of its own global total through IMAX screens alone, and IMAX CEO Rich Gelfond said the film's trajectory has been difficult to predict even for the company itself.
A Blockbuster Summer for Hollywood

"The Odyssey" and "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" have combined for more than $2.1 billion at the global box office between them, and industry watchers say the pair are pushing Hollywood toward a domestic box office total above $4 billion for only the second time since the pandemic — a mark last hit in 2023 thanks to "Barbenheimer."
With the film continuing to hold strong in its third weekend and IMAX 70mm showtimes reportedly sold out into September, analysts expect "The Odyssey" to keep climbing well into the fall.

title: New Documents From Liam Payne Investigation Surface Nearly Two Years After His Death
excerpt: More than 3,000 documents and photographs from the Argentine police investigation into Liam Payne's 2024 death have reportedly been obtained by the Daily Mail, offering a fuller picture of his final hours at a Buenos Aires hotel.
body: Nearly two years after Liam Payne's death, newly surfaced material from the Argentine police investigation is offering a more detailed timeline of the former One Direction singer's last day. The Daily Mail reports it obtained more than 3,000 documents and photographs from the probe into his October 2024 fall from a third-floor hotel balcony in Buenos Aires.

Payne, 31, died after falling roughly 46 feet from his room at the CasaSur Palermo Hotel. Prosecutors previously said he had spent his final day drinking heavily and using drugs before hotel staff helped him back to his room from the lobby. A hotel employee had called emergency services shortly before his death, expressing concern that he could hurt himself.
What the New Material Shows

According to reporting on the documents, the material includes images from inside the hotel in the hours leading up to Payne's death, along with witness statements gathered as investigators worked to reconstruct his movements. Much of it corroborates the broader timeline prosecutors had already laid out in earlier statements, rather than introducing a dramatically different account.
Where the Legal Case Stands

Five people were charged in connection with Payne's death in the months following the incident, including a friend who had been with him earlier that day and two hotel employees. Investigators reviewed more than 800 hours of security footage along with Payne's phone records and messages as part of building the case, which prosecutors said showed at least four instances of drugs reaching him during his final days at the hotel. The case has continued to move through the Argentine courts since.
A Legacy That Continues Beyond the Headlines

Payne's death sent shockwaves through the music industry and his global fanbase, with tributes pouring in from his former One Direction bandmates and artists across the industry. As the investigation continues to unfold in public, fans and commentators alike have noted the difficult balance between public interest in the case and respect for a young life lost.

title: 'High School Musical' Costars Joe Serafini and Frankie Rodriguez Are Engaged
excerpt: The couple, who met filming Disney's 'High School Musical: The Musical: The Series,' announced their engagement to a wave of congratulations from their former castmates.
body: Joe Serafini and Frankie Rodriguez, who met while co-starring on Disney+'s "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series," announced their engagement on August 7, adding their names to a growing list of celebrity couples who got engaged this year.

The news brought an outpouring of support from their former castmates.
